item.author: Jennifer Ouellette
item.content:encoded: Those of us missing the John Wick universe can take heart, because Chad Stahelski—who created that franchise—is coming back early next year with a new dystopian action film. It's called (a Japanese term that means "death overwork"), and Lionsgate released a killer trailer that puts this film at the top of my list of "must see" movies of 2027.Dying from working too hard is a very real phenomenon, not just in Japan and much of Asia, but also in Sweden. The physical cause is usually stress-related heart attacks or strokes, as well as suicide ( in Japan). Writer/director Takashi Doscher has transported that concept to a grim, futuristic corporate Manhattan, specifically a company called Ikigai Technologies. Per the official premise: is an action-thriller set in a near-future Manhattan, where corporate loyalty and cultural tradition have reshaped everyday life. When a mysterious outsider infiltrates a powerful company after a worker’s death, he exposes the violent system hidden beneath its polished surface.Teo Yoo () stars as the aptly named Hiro, who is clearly out for vengeance against the offending corporation. The cast also includes Takehiro Hira, so memorable in the 2024 miniseries as well as Giancarlo Esposito, Cynthia Erivo, Bill Camp, Richard Harmon, Isabel May, and Show Kasamatsu.

item.content:encoded: There are optimistic plans for spaceflight, and then there are plans.AST SpaceMobile is a Texas-based, publicly traded company building very large satellites to provide direct-to-cell communications on Earth. But it has been having trouble finding rides to space. So on Friday, AST announced that it is developing a medium-lift rocket, named Blacklift, which will have the capacity to lift 20 metric tons to low-Earth orbit. Oh, and the company said it would start launching commercially in late 2028."The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owner's economics in the industry," said Abel Avellan, founder, chairman, and CEO of AST SpaceMobile, in a news release.

item.title: The Knicks have a bench guard conundrum
item.author: Michael Zeno
item.content:encoded: When you’re the defending champions, there are not many holistic things to complain about. Sure, the Knicks started 0-3 with a very unsettling offense, but all they needed was their medicine (the Nets and Bulls) to get back to .500?Worried about losing to Philadelphia twice in October? Joel Embiid’s plantar fasciitis has already acted up; calm down.Any “problems” this early in the season are either short-term, regarding the looming extension talks, or good problems, which are more conundrums than actual problems.The biggest of those conundrums has to do with the Knicks’ rotation, specifically with their copious amounts of guard depth.Jalen Brunson is the head of the snake, but after him? There are a lot of players with minutes who could fluctuate on any given night.Tyler Kolek and Jose Alvarado duel over backup ball-handler minutes. Jordan Clarkson and Deuce McBride grapple over bench two-guard minutes. Landry Shamet’s strong play is actively pushing starters Mikal Bridges and Josh Hart over their minutes with the three entrenched parts of the team’s nucleus.It does qualify as a good problem to have, as injuries will undoubtedly give each of these guys ample opportunity over the course of 82 games, but when they’re all healthy, like they are right now? It probably gives Mike Brown a bigger headache than watching Andre Drummond attempt layups.All of these guys provide something that the Knicks could use more of, but have warts that can limit their playing time.Kolek is the best true playmaker, but he’s a poor defender, and his jump shot has been consistent throughout his young NBA career. This basically also describes Alvarado, but the defense is better from the New York native. McBride has stretches where he’s the team’s best rate shooter and is a tremendously pesky point-of-attack defender… but is that not what the team is getting out of a taller two-guard in Shamet?Clarkson has been a sparkplug every game he’s played this year, but the 35-year-old showed his maddening inconsistency in his first year in New York.It’s created an extremely volatile rotation, which isn’t surprising when you have a coach who opened the year saying only five players on this team have minutes that are secured.Despite zero Knicks players averaging more than 33 minutes a game except Brunson (who’s at 34.1), only Shamet is averaging more than 18 minutes a game off the bench.McBride is at 17.5, Kolek is at 12.2, Alvarado is at 11.3, and Clarkson is at 9.9, but even these are deceiving.Kolek has played steady rotation minutes, but didn’t play at all in the first two games before Alvarado’s ankle injury. Alvarado played 16 and 11 minutes, got hurt, got benched after nine minutes on Monday, and was on track to be a DNP-CD against the Bulls on Wednesday.Clarkson’s gone from playing three, five, or eight minutes to his spurts of 15 and 17 in the two games against the Bulls and his 11 to spark the incredible fourth quarter against Brooklyn.McBride, who’s served as the Knicks’ sixth man for over two years now, has topped 17 minutes just twice. He played a season-low 11 minutes on Wednesday and hasn’t had a clear role.To get these guys more minutes, it would mean cutting minutes from Hart or Bridges. While both have their warts, and the latter continues to look somehow less involved than he was during his lowest moments last season, some of the Knicks’ best lineups are coming with them on the court… just separated.We’ve seen Brown deploy line changes significantly more in the early going, opting to sub in three or four players at a time to deploy uniform units, but that’s not helping how erratic this all feels.The depth is making players redundant on the court, especially with how unwise it is to run four-guard lineups in an NBA that’s prioritizing size and length more and more. And with the Knicks’ extremely shallow forward and center depth? This glut might have to be sorted out at the trade deadline. As much as McBride has shown his tremendous value to the Knicks over the course of his contract, if he isn’t going to play more, is it even a net positive to keep him for the playoff run?For now, it’s merely a conundrum that Coach Brown will be scratching his head over every game.By the time we hit February? Things better be sorting themselves out.

item.title: What happened in first Brazil F1 practice
item.author: Josh Suttill
item.content:encoded: Lando Norris edged the new Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli to top the first practice session at the Brazilian Grand Prix, as Colton Herta completed his F1 superlicence mission.Norris set the pace with a 1m11.717s, lapping just 0.082s quicker than Antonelli.McLaren is the only team that has brought upgrades to Brazil with a new front and rear wing, modified floor furniture and a beam wing.Max Verstappen (Red Bull), who complained of "unacceptable downshifts", and Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) made it four different teams in the top four, all within just over three tenths of a second.George Russell was fifth fastest ahead of Isack Hadjar's Red Bull.Gabriele Mini was the fastest of the six FP1-only rookies in seventh place for Alpine in his second successive FP1 outing, 0.852s off the pace and just under a tenth ahead of regular driver Franco Colapinto, who was ninth.On home soil, Gabriel Bortoleto's Audi was eighth between the two Alpine drivers while Liam Lawson rounded out the top 10 for Racing Bulls.McLaren's reserve driver Leonardo Fornaroli was 11th ahead of Haas's Ollie Bearman and Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso.Rafael Camara finished his first FP1 session in 18th place, eight and a half tenths behind Bearman, as he builds up slowly to his unexpected grand prix debut this weekend - replacing Esteban Ocon.Herta picked up the final point he needs to qualify for his F1 superlicence, as he surpassed the 100 kilometres of running required to earn the 40th and final point, when combined with his four other qualifying FP1 runs and his IndyCar results.Cadillac thought it was mission accomplished in Mexico until it emerged that its FIA-verified calculations included an error on IndyCar's website. That meant Herta needed another FP1 outing in Brazil to finally get him over the line, removing a key obstacle to him replacing Valtteri Bottas in 2027, should the team decide to do so.Bottas was 15th, and nine tenths quicker than Herta in FP1.Freddie Slater's second FP1 outing ended up being even shorter than his first, as he'd completed just seven laps before his Audi ground to a halt, bringing out an early red flag.It means Slater has been able to complete just 21 laps between his back-to-back first F1 practice outings in Mexico and Brazil.Ferrari's Dino Beganovic also had a disrupted FP1 session as he lost a lot of time to his team needing to change his floor mid-session. He ended up with just 11 laps, having been told to abort his soft tyre lap for a car problem.

item.title: TotalEnergies team survives as new three-year sponsor announcement imminent
item.author: laura.weislo@futurenet.com (Laura Weislo)
item.content:encoded: After months of uncertainty and the loss of half of their riders, the TotalEnergies squad have found new life, according to Ouest France.An official announcement from managers Jean-René Bernaudeau and Stéphane Heulot is expected on November 9, according to .At the time, Bernaudeau said, "We need to have ten riders under contract and a sponsor providing a bank guarantee before being interviewed in December to finalise the budget. The end of the month is obviously the deadline; we promised ourselves we wouldn't go beyond October 31st."Bernaudeau appears to have met that cutoff with the imminent announcement of a title sponsor for the next three years.However, the team will have to be aggressive in the transfer market over the next three years if they hope to rejoin the WorldTour in 2029, as they have lost their top points scorers during the uncertainty surrounding their future, some of whom have made a step up to the WorldTour.Their GC hopeful Jordan Jegat, who finished 10th overall in the Tour de France and won the Classic Grand Besançon Doubs in April, has already signed for Lidl-Trek. Classics specialist Anthony Turgis and Nicolas Breuillard have already inked deals with XDS Astana, and Alexandre Delettre, along with Emilien Jeannière, a podium finisher in the Scheldeprijs, and Sandy Dujardin left for Groupama-FDJ. Pierre Thierry signed with Cofidis.Meanwhile, Mathieu Burgaudeau, Thomas Bonnet and Mattéo Vercher jumped ship for ProTeam Burgos-Burpellet BH, while Lorrenzo Manzin, Geoffrey Bouchard and Fabien Greiller retired.Bernaudeau may yet hold on to Jason Tesson, winner of the Classic Var, who was their fourth-best scorer in 2026, and Tour of Mentougou winner Joris Delbove, who are among the 14 riders who have not yet announced their 2027 contracts.The outfit have a long history in the peloton, having been founded in 1986. They were briefly a professional team as Castorama before returning to a development programme. In 2000, Bernaudeau landed Bonjour as a title sponsor and, under that banner and later as Brioches La Boulangère, Bouygues Télécom and Team Europcar became fixtures in the ProTour, the predecessor to the WorldTour.Thomas Voeckler's ten-day stint in the maillot jaune in 2004 was the team's biggest highlight, but by 2009, the team were forced to drop out of the top tier and almost disbanded in 2010 as they struggled to find a sponsor until Europcar came along.The team brought on Direct Énergie as a sponsor in 2019 and, as TotalEnergies, signed superstar Peter Sagan with high ambitions of rejoining the WorldTour, but the three-time world champion won only a single race for the French outfit, a stage of the Tour de Suisse in 2022, and the team did not meet the promotion criteria by the end of 2025.In 2026, the team fell short of the top three ProTeams, being beaten by Pinarello-Q36.5, Tudor and Cofidis, so they will not earn automatic invitations to the Grand Tours. However, they remain eligible for wildcard entries as they made the top 30 in the UCI Team Rankings, and as the fourth-best ProTeam, will be invited to the one-day WorldTour events.The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: James Paxton
item.author: John Griffin
item.content:encoded: After the 2018 season, the Yankees’ pitching staff looked thin. Young ace Luis Severino gave them a top-flight starter atop the rotation, and Masahiro Tanaka was a more-than-capable No. 3 starter with a tendency of stepping up in big spots, but Sonny Gray and Domingo Germán were disasters while CC Sabathia and J.A. Happ were on the wrong side of 45. Compared to the Boston Red Sox — led by Chris Sale, Nathan Eovaldi, and David Price — and the three-headed monster of Justin Verlander, Gerrit Cole, and Dallas Keuchel in Houston, it was clear that the Bombers had a lot of catching up to do in the arms race.To that end, the Yankees opened the 2018-2019 offseason by swinging a deal for James Paxton, sending a package centered on top pitching prospect Justus Sheffield to the Seattle Mariners. November 6, 1988 (Richmond, British Columbia, Canada)2019-20Born and raised in British Columbia, Paxton made a name for himself on the Canadian youth baseball circuit, ultimately helping to lead Team Canada to a bronze medal at the 2006 World Junior Baseball Championship. Following his high school career, the Big Maple took his talents to the United States, joining the University of Kentucky. Between his performance with the Wildcats (first as a reliever, then as a starter) and with the summer Alaska Baseball League, he quickly found himself on the radar of Major League ballclubs. After a junior year in which he struck out 115 batters in 78.1 innings, he was drafted by the Toronto Blue Jays with the 37th overall pick of the 2009 draft (the compensation Toronto received when the Yankees signed A.J. Burnett). Unfortunately, they were unable to come a deal, and Paxton opted to return to Kentucky for his senior year… that is, until the Blue Jays told the media that they had been negotiating with Scott Boras, not with Paxton’s family. Back in the pre-NIL days, hiring an agent changed your status from an amateur to a pro, and he was declared ineligible; an attempt to sue in order to be reinstated led nowhere, and eventually, Paxton withdrew from Kentucky to begin his professional career.Paxton spent the 2010 season with the Grand Prairie AirHogs, an American Association team which allowed him to retain draft eligibility. On the back of a solid, albeit unspectacular, performance there, he was selected by the Seattle Mariners in the fourth round of the 2010 draft. After a lengthy negotiation, he finally put pen to paper in March 2011, and began what would be a rapid ascent through the minor leagues. He reached Double-A by the end of 2011, received an invitation to spring training in 2012, and finally made his Major League debut on September 7, 2013.Thanks to a strong cup of coffee in 2013, Paxton began the 2014 season in the Seattle rotation, where he would spend the next five seasons. Unfortunately, he fell into a rather predictable pattern. When healthy, he was one of the league’s premier pitchers: his 13.2 fWAR from 2014 to 2018 ranked 26th out of the 88 starters who went at least 550 innings, and his 18.8 K-BB% ranked 14th — just one-tenth of a percentage point behind Cole and three-tenths behind Tanaka. And on May 8, 2018, he became just the second Canadian-born pitcher to throw a no-hitter in baseball history — a testament to his ability.However, Paxton was hardly healthy for a full season: he made more than 20 starts just twice in that span, having hit the IL with a lat strain in 2014, a strained tendon in his finger in 2015, a forearm strain and a pec strain in 2017, and back inflammation and a forearm strain in 2018.When the Yankees acquired Paxton that winter, they gambled that his ability on the mound would be worth the risk of his lengthy injury history. In 2019, that was absolutely the case. In the year where pretty much every member of the Yankees spent time on the injured list, the oft-injured pitcher put together the healthiest season of his career, making 29 starts and spending just a few weeks of May on the shelf.Despite a nasty tendency to surrender home runs in the first inning, Paxton anchored the Yankees rotation, and when the Yankees needed him most in October, he delivered. Getting the ball with the team down 3-1 in the ALCS and having dropped three consecutive games, Paxton shook off two less-than-stellar postseason starts to shut down the Astros lineup, striking out nine and allowing just one run in six innings to send the series back to Houston. Sure, things didn’t get any better from there, but that’s another story (and not any of Paxton’s fault, either).As good as things went for Paxton in 2019, however, that’s how bad 2020 went. On February 5th, he underwent lumbar surgery, which would have sidelined him for 3-4 months if the season hadn’t been delayed because of the pandemic. Although he made it back in time for the late-July Opening Day, he put together the worst season of his career, posting a 6.64 ERA in 20.1 innings across five starts before hitting the shelf again, this time with a left flexor tendon strain — perhaps the reason for the diminished velocity that made him suddenly very hittable.Perhaps unsurprisingly, the Yankees opted to let Paxton walk in free agency, and he returned to the Seattle Mariners on a one-year deal. After just 1.1 innings, though, he left the game with an elbow injury, and later that week, it was announced that he needed Tommy John surgery.A free agent again that winter, Paxton returned to the AL East joining the Red Sox on a one-year deal with a two-year club option and a one-year player option. A lat tear ended his attempt at a comeback in 2022, prompting Boston to reject the club option and Paxton to accept the player option. Due to a right hamstring strain, he began the 2023 season on the IL, and finally, on May 12, 2023, he made his Boston debut. Over the next two months, he pitched well, posting a 3.34 ERA in 13 starts in his first bit of extended action since 2020. Boston floated Paxton at the deadline, but ultimately held onto him in an attempt to make a bid for a Wild Card spot after a dominant July. That would turn out to be a mistake for everyone involved: a mediocre August and terrible October sent the Red Sox to the basement of the AL East, and Paxton battled inconsistency before being shut down with knee inflammation at the start of September.Paxton signed with the Dodgers on a one-year deal in January 2024, a contract that was originally $11 million but reworked and lowered to $7 million with playing-time incentives due to unspecified health issues. He made 18 starts for Los Angeles, helping them deal with a rash of injuries to the rotation, before being surprisingly and unceremoniously designated for assignment to make room for River Ryan and Clayton Kershaw on the active and 40-man rosters, respectively. The Red Sox claimed him off waivers, and after three starts, he suffered a calf tear that ended his season.The Big Maple retired from Major League Baseball after the 2024 season, but that wouldn’t be the last time we saw him on a mound. Paxton accepted the invitation to pitch for Team Canada during the 2026 World Baseball Classic. Working out of the bullpen, he touched 97 mph on his fastball in two appearances, including 2.2 scoreless frames against Cuba to advance out of the group stage. Despite potential interest from pro teams, Paxton has reiterated that he will remain retired. Aside from spending time with his family, he is in the process of completing the business degree he abandoned at the University of Kentucky when he was declared ineligible more than 15 years ago; after that, he intends to pursue a Master’s degree in sports psychology.Happy birthday to James Paxton!See more of the “Yankees Birthday of the Day” series here.

item.title: 'If you like it, then why would you stop?' – Approaching his 40s, Wout Poels continues into 19th and final pro season with Unibet Rose Rockets in 2027
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: Wout Poels will continue racing into his 19th season as a professional in 2027 with Unibet Rose Rockets, the French-registered ProTeam confirmed on Friday. The 39-year-old joined the Rockets at the start of 2026, and after maintaining his love of training and racing, particularly at the Giro d'Italia – the team's first and his 26th Grand Tour – and his high levels of performance, Poels didn't want to hang up his wheels just yet. Born out of a YouTube channel and owned by Bas Tietema, Josse Wester, and Devin van der Wiel, the Rockets are approaching their fifth season in the pro peloton, with Poels part of a 26-rider roster that also includes Dylan Groenewegen. In 2027, they will look to secure invites to the Giro and a first Tour de France.Poels' extension was confirmed in an accompanying video featuring him and Tietema at the former's fan club cafe in his home village of Blitterswijck, where the pair discussed plans for 2027 and played darts."Now I have to say, because of the Giro, it triggered a little bit more. It was a really nice three weeks and a really, really good level," said Poels. "The most important thing is that I really like to do it. I like to train. I like to race. I like to do training camps. If you like it, then why would you stop? And the level is still there. That's the most important one."I imagine if I would have really did shit in the Giro and you get all the time dropped, you never go in a break, you never make a result, then I think I would not continue. I also like to be in the mix to do results, but even at a small race like Sibiu Tour, I was fourth in the GC and then second in the mountain stage – it's not the biggest race, but I still enjoy to race and get a result."Poels will turn 40 on October 1 next, and while this is supposed to be his final year of racing, he still didn't rule out potentially keeping going into a 20th year. "Is this really the last one?" asked Tietema. "Normally, yes… The door is always a little bit open," said Poels. A former Liège-Bastogne-Liège winner, Tour de France stage winner, and Vuelta a España stage winner, Poels isn't landing the same calibre of results he was in his prime years at Team Sky and Bahrain Victorious, but he's still been able to land several impressive top 10s for the Rockets. Poels finished in the top 10 of two stages at the Giro, including on the brutal mountain day to Pila on stage 14, where he was eighth and only lost out to the top GC favourites. He also finished fourth on GC at the Sibiu Tour in Romania, and seventh overall at the Arctic Race of Norway. "The Giro; that's the highest level of the WorldTour, and it's really nice to perform there, especially on the mountain days to do top ten there from the peloton, that gives me a really good feeling," he said."OK, for me, I did, I think, 26 Grand Tours. But then I really come to my best after one week of racing, and I still feel that I get less fatigue. "The WorldTour teams and Pro Teams, just to be in the top ten is always really high level. If you really want to perform there, then you need to be 100% ready."But it's exactly that process which the Dutchman is still enjoying, having trained at altitude for the Giro this past season. Not only can he operate as a climbing leader, but Poels – as one of the most iconic super domestiques of the Team Sky era – is one of the most valuable riders for the Rockets' young talents to learn from. For now, his win tally reads the same as his Grand Tour appearances at 26, but he's looking to bump them both up to at least 27 in 2027. It would maintain a run of winning a race on every team he's raced for as a pro, and a streak of starting a Grand Tour in every season that extends back to 2011 when he was on Vacansoleil-DCM – this was the season when he finished second atop the Alto l'Angliru behind Juan Jose Cobo at the Vuelta. "I really would like to win a race for the team because I didn't do that last year. I was close to it, but I didn't do it," said Poels. "That would be really nice, also for myself, just for my stats to say that I won a race in every team. But I just want to approach it like last year; have a good time, go to some nice races, perform well, try to do good GCs, just make good results. That's what I like to do."The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: What’s happening with Cadillac F1 buyout talks amid Fenway interest
item.author: Darren Cox
item.content:encoded: Once upon a time, if you wanted to know who was buying into a Formula 1 team you could ask the bloke who owned it over coffee in the paddock.Such is the way ownerships are now structured and managed in F1 there may only be one person in the paddock that actually knows something about the sale, someone with a freshly signed contract who appears to have let something slip on Thursday. When I recently dug into who actually owns each F1 team, the distance we have travelled from the owner-operator days became very clear. The person running the team, the company whose name is above the garage, and the people who ultimately control the money can be three very different things.That matters when considering the potential sale of a stake in Cadillac's F1 team.There has been plenty of talk around the Austin and Mexico paddocks. But the reporting that has moved the story forward has come from American sporting and financial circles, led by Sportico, followed by the likes of the Wall Street Journal. The Race's journalists have been seeking confirmation in Brazil. That does not mean the answers are in Brazil.I have been told that these negotiations are being handled personally by Walter and a very small circle around him. People working at Silverstone, at the American facilities, or in the garage at Interlagos, could quite reasonably know very little about it.Cadillac has a struggling racing team and urgent challenges on track to resolve. Its owner has a collection of businesses and challenges of his own to manage, including federal investigations involving his insurance businesses.That is why Cadillac's stance that nothing has doesn’t mean that nothing is .My sources have indicated, for months, that a sale process is under way. Getting formal confirmation or anyone willing to speak on the record has proved rather harder, as is often the way with these things. The remaining question is what the outcome of that process will be. That is where the interest lies.The least surprising part is that somebody wants to buy in.Fenway among the prospective buyersWalter has meanwhile been selling sporting assets, including his interests in the Lakers and Chelsea, against the backdrop of reported financial pressures and federal investigations involving his insurance businesses. TWG denies wrongdoing. That wider situation matters far more to this transaction than Cadillac's latest qualifying position.It does not follow that Walter needed to begin by putting up a "for sale" sign. Prospective investors have been knocking on his door. In his circumstances, those conversations would be difficult to ignore.The Guardian has reported talks about a majority purchase by Fenway Sports Group, which owns Liverpool FC and the Boston Red Sox among others. The preference on Walter's side appears to be a minority sale that allows him to retain control.A preference is not a completed deal. But the distinction matters.Lawrence Stroll provides a useful example. As we explored in the ownership article, he has brought successive investors into Aston Martin while retaining commanding voting and governance rights. Economic ownership and control are different things.An owner can take money off the table, bring in another investor and still decide who sits in his second F1 seat. So, the percentage sold will tell only part of Cadillac's story. The rights attached to those shares may tell us considerably more.It is generally understood that Walter holds 67%, Dan Towriss 3% and General Motors 30%. Those figures have not been publicly confirmed and they do not tell us what approvals or protections GM has.That is a significant unknown.When I interviewed Flavio Briatore about Otro Capital's proposed sale of its 24% Alpine stake, he made a practical point about Renault's position. Its formal veto period ran until September. But who would commit hundreds of millions of dollars to a minority stake without a workable relationship with the majority shareholder?A date passing on a contract does not remove the need to get along.GM's position at Cadillac is different and we should not assume identical rights. But any buyer would need to understand its relationship with the manufacturer whose name, investment and long-term commitment are central to the proposition.Seemingly well-informed in such matters, Sergio Perez offered a reminder of that in Brazil on Thursday, speaking to media including The Race.Perez pointed to GM as "one of the biggest manufacturers", before considering whether the TWG investors wanted to "get some of their investment back"."But I don't think it will change any structure at all," he said.Having just signed a new long-term contract, Perez would have had every reason to ask what a sale might mean for the team before committing. He sounds unsure about why the investors would sell, but rather more certain about what happens afterwards. He may know more than most in Brazil. And that last line may have just let it show.Naturally, there are plenty of other people being linked to said new structure. An apprentice mechanic's job could become available in F1 and somebody would mention Christian Horner. His name appearing in this conversation is therefore hardly a revelation. More interestingly I have also heard considerably wilder suggestions involving prominent paddock figures. As far as I can establish, those have not developed into firm outcomes. Yet. Of the names reported, Fenway Sports Group, I've been assured, looks the most likely to progress. Why Fenway's interest deserves attentionThe very American nature of Fenway is of particular interest.Informally, GM and senior management have been very pleased with the particularly strong response when Cadillac leans into its American identity. That has strengthened the appetite for an American driver, with Colton Herta increasingly central to that ambition, and for an American investment partner. The Race's audience data backs up this assertion. Our US audience figures spike on Cadillac and Herta stories. Obvious but important. The process of getting Herta into F1 has, in my view, exposed the inexperience around the decision-making at a sporting level within the team. That deserves a piece of its own, which I will return to if, as seems increasingly likely, he is confirmed around the Las Vegas Grand Prix as Cadillac's second driver for 2027. For now, the decision remains publicly unresolved and Valtteri Bottas has been told there is still a route to him staying.The commercial logic is easy enough to see. An American manufacturer, an American driver, and an investor experienced in American sport make a coherent proposition to sponsors and supporters.Herta would still have to deliver behind the wheel. But the appeal of that combination helps explain why the driver discussion and the ownership discussion belong in the same article.For Walter, the task is now to realise as much value while preserving as much influence as possible. For GM, it is to ensure the funding and stability is in place to support its long-term ambitions.The negotiations that settle those questions will tell us more about Cadillac's future than anything said outside its garage this weekend.

item.title: 'I think she has grown a lot mentally' – Lars Boom highlights reason for Demi Vollering's stunning season, outlines 2027 goals
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: FDJ United-SUEZ manager Lars Boom has outlined Demi Vollering's main goals for the 2027 season and talked about what went right in a stunningly successful 2026 campaign.Vollering enjoyed her most successful season yet, with wins at the Tour of Flanders, Liège-Bastogne-Liège, the Giro d'Italia Women, Tour de France Femmes, and the World and European Championships, among 16 victories.She added another trophy to her collection on Monday, taking home the Keetie van Oosten-Hage trophy as the best Dutch female cyclist of the year. It's her second time winning the award, having previously triumphed in 2023.At the ceremony in Utrecht, Boom told about Vollering's 2027 goals, with her schedule likely to follow a familiar pattern."Well, I think the Tour de France again. And defending her world title," Boom said of her top priorities for next season. Her early season goals and starting point have yet to be defined, however."She will ride some Classics and maybe the Giro again. It's a bit obvious, of course, but I think the Tour and the World Championships will be major milestones again."Vollering has been in the USA in recent weeks, travelling through California and Oregon and taking part in events and rides with sponsors Specialized, Red Bull, and visiting Nike HQ in Portland.Attention will soon turn to the 2027 season, though, and renewed hostilities with rivals including Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney at Lidl-Trek, new Movistar pairing Paula Blasi and Marlen Reusser, Visma-Lease a Bike leader Pauline Ferrand-Prévot, and UAE Team L'IMAD's Elisa Longo Borghini, among others.She beat all of them in 2026, and Boom hinted at what she did right."I think she has grown a lot mentally. If I take the Giro as an example, she was quite nervous back then," Boom said."In the Tour, however, there was total calm, and we basically didn't say anything on the bus or just before the start. That really made a world of difference."The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: Yankees 2026 Roster Report Cards: Fernando Cruz
item.author: Jonathan Farrar
item.content:encoded: One of the most beautiful parts of baseball is how many different personal journeys we fans get to learn about as players chase their dreams. Fernando Cruz’s story aside, let’s dive into the season that earned him a B- from the staff here at Pinstripe Alley.Cruz’s 2026 really started at the World Baseball Classic, representing Team Puerto Rico. After rejoining the Yankees, he picked up where he left off last season as a trusted member of Aaron Boone’s bullpen. From there, it became a story of two halves. 61 games, 54.2 IP, 3.13 ERA (135 ERA+), 4.17 FIP, 4.39 xFIP, 28.6 K%, 13.7 BB%, 0.0 fWAR, 1.2 rWAR, 4-6 record Arbitration-eligibleBefore the All-Star break, Cruz was excellent. He was a borderline All-Star, striking out 50 batters over 40 innings while holding opponents to a .191 batting average. His best month of the season was May, when he appeared in 14 games and posted a 1.02 WHIP while allowing just two earned runs over 13.2 innings. He was one of the more dependable pieces out of the bullpen during the first half of what was an underrated unit.The key to this effectiveness was his splitter, which he deployed 51.3 percent of the time. He paired that pitch with a four-seamer, sweeper, and sinker to keep hitters off-balance. The splitter continued to be his best weapon, generating a 52 percent whiff rate and limiting hitters to a .161 average against it. After the break, however, his performance began to slip. Something seemed off as Cruz started losing some control in late July, and August became his roughest month of the season. He posted a 6.75 ERA over eight innings, allowing six home runs and four walks. Following a blown save against Houston on August 25th, the Yankees announced that Cruz had suffered a partial tear of his right ulnar collateral ligament, and he landed on the injured list the following day.The ultimate team guy, Cruz opted to pursue a non-surgical approach after receiving a second opinion with the hope he could make it back in 2026. He received a cortisone shot and started rehabbing trying to find his way back into the mix for the postseason. However, a month after landing on the injured list, the Yankees transferred Cruz to the 60-day injured list on September 25th, ending his chances of returning during the 2026 season. On the season, Cruz had some impressive underlying numbers. He ranked in the 91st percentile in average exit velocity and the 99th percentile in whiff rate. He also landed in the 82nd percentile in xERA, the 88th percentile in strikeout rate, and the 85th percentile in extension. However, his hard-hit rate ranked in just the 22nd percentile, and his walk rate was in the third percentile. The right-hander was also effective against left-handed hitters holding them to a .180 batting average.Losing Cruz after the Trade Deadline was less than ideal, especially with the Yankees having few options capable of replacing his production internally, which led to the Michael Fulmer experience. As the page turns to a new season, with the injury question mark hovering over him, Cruz becomes an interesting offseason decision for the Yankees.The team has until November 20th to tender him a contract for the 2027 season. Depending on the outlook for his elbow, it would not surprise me to see the Yankees retain him and try to work out a deal before arbitration. Given the injury uncertainty, it could be a buy-low opportunity for the club, provided they believe he can return to form and he is willing to accept a similar salary to last season. However, professional baseball is a business and the team might opt to use the money and roster spot they would spend on Cruz elsewhere this offseason.Personally, I gave Cruz a B for this season, and in hindsight, I feel that might have been a touch low. What grade would you assign Cruz, and what are your thoughts on him in pinstripes in 2027?See more of the Yankees Roster Report Card series here.

item.title: No more Cybertrucks; Musk moves on from the angular metallic flop
item.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
item.content:encoded: Elon’s Edsel is no more. Last night, Tesla CEO Elon Musk revealed on social media that his car company is ending its failed attempt to wrest control of the American pickup truck market. The Cybertruck will cease production in the middle of 2027, liberating that space in Tesla’s cavernous factory for other uses—more Cybercabs, most likely.Musk first revealed the Cybertruck in late 2019, back when Tesla was still trading at a theoretically understandable price-to-earning ratio. The pickup's unusual angular shape owed more to low-res video game models than any concessions to practicality. At the time, Musk made fanciful claims that the truck would use a stainless steel monocoque construction, telling his audience that “the body and bed don’t do anything useful” on a normal truck. While some race cars use carbon-fiber monocoques for strength and lightness, making a pickup truck with a stainless steel monocoque chassis would only make sense if someone had an awful lot of stainless steel lying around and needed something to do with it all.The truck was supposed to go on sale for less than $40,000, and Tesla made its usual stratospheric sales predictions that (had they been accurate) the bare metal EVs would be as ubiquitous as the Model 3 and Y.

item.content:encoded: ‘Low-hire, low-fire’ labor market shows sluggish growth but few layoffs, with an interest rate hike expected in DecemberThe US added 165,000 jobs to the economy in October, a sign of resilience in the labor market amid ongoing war in the Middle East and inflation, according to new data released on Friday.Economists had said the labor market has been stuck in a “low-hire, low-fire” state, in which job growth is sluggish but layoffs also remain low, but October’s data surpassed economist expectations. The unemployment rate went down slightly to 4.1%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported.Continue reading...

item.title: Rocket Report: Artemis II literally tore through the atmosphere; New Glenn delay
item.author: Stephen Clark
item.content:encoded: Welcome to Edition 9.18 of the Rocket Report! Blue Origin packed a lot of news into one afternoon Thursday with the reveal of a new kick stage for the New Glenn rocket, a new rocket engine design, and the minor and widely expected delay for New Glenn's return-to-flight mission from December until January. The reconstruction of Blue Origin's wrecked launch pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida, continues apace after a catastrophic explosion nearly six months ago. There's a lot of pent-up demand from NASA, Amazon, and the Space Force for Blue Origin to get New Glenn back in action.As always, we welcome reader submissions, and if you don't want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar.SpaceX vets work on water-fed propulsion. Three brothers who worked at SpaceX in the Falcon 9 era are now building satellites that run on water, a potentially harvestable resource on the Moon and found all over the Solar System, Ars reports. In late 2022, the three Carlisle brothers founded Argo Space to build infrastructure in space. Their vision was not just in-space transportation but also removing the need to use propellants from Earth to move around the heavens. Argo Space's satellites will use water not only as a propellant, but also as a coolant and radiation shield.

item.title: McLaren's 2027 F1 front wing breaks cover in Brazil
item.author: Jon Noble
item.content:encoded: McLaren’s new front wing, which will be the same concept it launches its 2027 Formula 1 car with, has been revealed at the Brazilian Grand Prix.As part of an end-of-season push by the Woking-based squad to deliver continuous improvements to its MCL40, the squad has brought its latest upgrades to Interlagos.This includes tweaks to its floor, an updated rear wing, but also a front wing that will form the starting point for next season’s MCL41.The front wing is a change of concept for the team as it features many revisions across the spectrum of wing elements.The attachment point for the main plane and the endplate has been revised to now run across the lower edge – where it marries up with the refined outboard element.The attachment between the nose and the main plane has been adjusted to sit on the second flap now rather than the mainplane, while the new wing also features an adjustment in the height of the flap elements.Speaking ahead of the weekend, McLaren explained that the changes delivered were about both delivering more downforce and improving car balance.Chief technical officer of aerodynamics Peter Prodromou also made clear that these changes were the launchpad for its 2027 project.“The season isn't over yet: these upgrades are designed to improve the car now and help us in our fight for third in the championship,” he explained.“While the learning we take from these upgrades will feed into next year’s development, we also expect to carry over the concept of the new front wing into the launch specification of next year’s car.”

item.title: ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted
item.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
item.content:encoded: Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 resultThe African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to voters turning away from the party.Continue reading...

item.title: Marquez quickest as Qatar MotoGP weekend kicks off
item.author: Valentin Khorounzhiy
item.content:encoded: MotoGP championship leader Marc Marquez led the way in the opening practice session of the Qatar Grand Prix, heading Marco Bezzecchi by a tenth of a second.Marquez led virtually the entire session on the dusty Lusail track, and ended up on a 1m52.278s. He never fitted a spare rear tyre - but neither did virtually anyone else, with no incentive to use up any of the valuable rubber in the less-representative daytime session (compared to Friday afternoon practice, the sprint and the grand prix all taking place in the evening under the lights).Fabio Di Giannantonio was third behind Marquez and Bezzecchi, four tenths down on the leader.Pedro Acosta was fourth as the lead KTM, but his RC16 seemed to either fail or run out of fuel in the end as he had to pull over to the side of the track.Jorge Martin, who had withdrawn from the Sepang weekend last time out due to his wrist fracture from Phillip Island, had a livelier start here, logging 16 laps and placing fifth.With the Yamaha riders absent as the manufacturer elected to skip Qatar, a total of 18 riders took part. Honda's new stand-in Jake Dixon was last of them, after crashing on his very first flying lap.But Dixon was just 3.1s off the pace in the end, so will have zero trouble clearing MotoGP's 105-percent pace rule for race eligibility.There was another crash early in the session, for KTM's Brad Binder, who likewise returned to action shortly.1 Marc Marquez (Ducati) 1m52.278s2 Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia) +0.110s3 Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Ducati) +0.413s4 Pedro Acosta (KTM) +0.677s5 Jorge Martin (Aprilia) +0.734s6 Pecco Bagnaia (Ducati) +0.793s7 Raul Fernandez (Trackhouse Aprilia) +0.911s8 Luca Marini (Honda) +0.952s9 Franco Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati) +1.028s10 Johann Zarco (LCR Honda) +1.084s11 Alex Marquez (Gresini Ducati) +1.263s12 Fermin Aldeguer (Gresini Ducati) +1.339s13 Brad Binder (KTM) +1.353s14 Iker Lecuona (Gresini Ducati) +1.432s15 Maverick Vinales (Tech3 KTM) +1.447s16 Diogo Moreira (LCR Honda) +1.791s17 Enea Bastianini (Tech3 KTM) +1.965s18 Jake Dixon (Honda) +3.148s

item.title: Should the Yankees non-tender Luis Gil?
item.author: Andrés Chávez
item.content:encoded: In 2024, New York Yankees right-hander Luis Gil impressed with a brilliant first half and a full campaign worthy of the American League Rookie of the Year Award. At that point, the Bombers thought they had unearthed another pitching gem, controllable for multiple years on the cheap.A severe lat strain in 2025 and shoulder issues in 2026 have hampered his progress and affected his fastball velocity and command, though. Last year, he posted a 3.32 ERA in 57 innings, but with very ugly peripherals. This season, the wheels completely fell off. The shoulder woes limited him to 39.1 innings between the majors and the minors. He finished with a 4.61 ERA and a rough 7.12 FIP in 27.1 MLB frames, with 18 walks and 17 strikeouts.The right-hander started to transition to a bullpen role during the season, which could actually represent his firmest, most concrete way into the team’s plans. With the non-tender deadline looming on November 20th, however, the Yankees will have to make a decision. Is holding onto Gil worth the headache? The right-hander is projected to get a modest raise in his first year of arbitration, to $2.3 million, according to MLB Trade Rumors. Money, in this case, is not the primary issue, though.Is Gil good or promising enough to warrant a place in the team’s future plans? Well, it will entirely depend on his ability to thrive out of the bullpen, which could be both his short and long-term home.The concept of Gil as a multi-inning reliever is certainly enticing. Potentially increased velocity and not as much wear and tear on his shoulder sound excellent for his long-term prospects, but he does have short-term goals: looking good on the mound and getting closer to that 2024 version of himself, regardless of role. He was a completely different pitcher back then:He is currently pitching for Tigres Del Licey in the Dominican Republic League, and boasts a solid 1.50 ERA in six frames, spanning over three games. The problem? He has issued six walks against seven strikeouts. Control has never been Gil’s calling card, but anything that starts with a five next to his BB/9 stat would represent a big problem.The Yankees would probably love to trade Gil, hoping to get something in return for his name value and the fact that he won the award for the league’s best rookie just two years ago. They are probably dangling his name in the market as we speak. If they can’t reach a deal with any team, they will need to make a decision. They can give their promising, yet erratic right-hander one last chance, probably in the bullpen, or they could choose to cut ties and not tender him a contract, making him free to sign with any squad.Complicating matters is the fact that Gil does not have any minor league options remaining. The next time the Yankees want to remove him from their 40-man roster, they will need to put him through waivers and risk losing him for nothing. If the Yankees can’t find a deal for him, they could opt to keep him around and try the bullpen experiment full-time to see if he can give them anything there, considering that it’s an area of need at the moment. It’s hard to see him sticking over the long term unless something drastically changes, though.

item.title: 'Miraculous' – Tadej Pogačar's heart rate data and sleep scores revealed in new documentary
item.author: Patrick Fletcher
item.content:encoded: Tadej Pogačar has a resting heart rate of 38 beats per minute, a heart rate variability of 100, and a 'miraculous' prowess for sleep, according to new up-to-date figures revealed by his physiological data tracking sponsor, Whoop. The numbers were disclosed in the first of a new documentary series on Eurosport, TNT Sports and HBO Max, titled ‘Anatomy of a G.O.A.T’, which aims to "decode the science behind the greatest athletes of all-time". The first documentary, which airs on Saturday, looks to piece together the puzzle of Pogačar’s startling superiority over the rest of the peloton. "Tadej’s resting heart rate, right, which is a very nice kind of global picture of your cardiorespiratory fitness, is 38," says Whoop’s Global Head of Human Performance, Kristen Holmes. Holmes states that the average resting heart rate for a male of Pogačar’s, 27, age is 59, while also revealing that the other 27-year-old riders on UAE Team Emirates-XRG are a good bit higher."The average of the six other teammates is 42. He’s about four beats per minute slower than his teammates. And what this points to is a more efficient cardiorespiratory system, because he’s got this very efficient engine."Pogačar’s resting heart rate of 38, while putting him a cut above his teammates, is not other-worldly like the 28bpm reportedly associated with another five-time Tour de France winner, Miguel Indurain. Earlier this year, Pogačar’s top Classics rival, Mathieu van der Poel revealed his resting heart rate was the same, on average, at 38, though he noted the lowest he’d recorded was 34. Heart rate variability – or a 'readiness indicator'Whoop, as with Van der Poel earlier in the year, also revealed Pogačar’s heart rate variability, which is a measure of the variation in time taken between heart beats, measured in milliseconds over a long period of time, such as overnight. It tracks the balance of the body’s autonomic nervous system but is described by Whoop in layman’s terms as a “readiness indicator”, with a higher HRV indicating superior physical fitness and recovery. "The more variable that time interval, the more kind of ready you are to take on load," says Holmes. "So Tadej, his heart rate variability is 100. The other six riders on his team, their average is in the 80s. So he has to work less hard for the same output."While the average HRV for active individuals is said to be between 40 and 65, Pogačar’s score of 100 pales in comparison with Van der Poel’s claimed HRV of 200."I’m really high in HRV," Van der Poel said earlier this year. "I think it’s a bit genetical, but fitness is important also. For sure, it’s something that makes me stronger and better recovered."The HRV scores tie into the most important factor when it comes to recovery: sleep, and here is another area where Pogačar is said to be "remarkable". Whoop’s wearable technology monitors riders overnight, and gives them a ‘sleep score’ in the morning. "Sleep consistency is when you go to bed and when you wake up, and the stability of that. And it’s expressed as a percentage. So on a scale of 0 to 100, again, you know, Tadej is 84%," says Holmes in the ‘Anatomy of a G.O.A.T’ documentary."Over the course of the 2026 Tour de France, none of the cyclists on the UAE team had sleep consistency that compared to Tadej’s 84%. They were mostly in the 70 to 80% range," adds Research Scientist Gregory Grosicki. "One of the things we see very clearly in our data is that, when our members and even our elite athletes on Whoop do very high intensity efforts, the quality of their sleep tends to suffer. But with Tadej, he takes that even a step further. Going into the [Tour de France], he was sleeping about 7 hours. During the entire 2026 Tour de France, he was sleeping 8 hours. Miraculous. He’s sleeping more. He’s sleeping more regularly."Asked about his sleep skills, Pogačar said: “I’m not a big hour sleeper, but if you eat clean and good for the dinner, I think it’s the biggest impact on the sleep then. And yeah, you just need to be relaxed and be organised for the next morning.”Pogačar's powers of recovery were further underlined by his former coach Iñigo San Millán."He has an astonishing ability to recover," said the Spaniard. "We did some metabolic testing. We can see between 1000 and 2000 metabolic parameters, and one of them is ability to recover. Some of the antioxidant parameters are very important for recovery. When we saw his results, Tadej was far ahead of everyone else."'Anatomy of a G.O.A.T' premieres on Saturday November 7 and will be available to stream in the UK, US, and Europe on The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. Subscribe for unlimited access to our comprehensive news coverage, industry-leading CN Labs testing, expert columnists, and so much more. Plus, the Cyclingnews app means you can stay up-to-date wherever you go!

item.title: How much has bad luck really cost George Russell in F1 2026?
item.author: Josh Suttill
item.content:encoded: George Russell says he's only had six race weekends without an issue in a bruising 2026 Formula 1 season.But, on a Brazilian Grand Prix weekend where he's facing another grid penalty, does his claim stack up, and how much does bad luck explain his clear defeat to Kimi Antonelli? Antonelli has destroyed his Mercedes team-mate Russell this year, winning nine races to Russell's three and wrapping up the title with four rounds to spare last weekend in Mexico.Facing the media for the first time in Brazil since that crushing title loss was confirmed, Russell admitted to "feel[ing] a bit exhausted this season of constantly picking myself back up". "When you get kicked to the ground, you pick yourself back up, then you get kicked down again, you pick yourself back up, and I was hoping to do that maybe twice in the season, not every other weekend really," he said. "When you get to a point of this season, you're away from home three weeks in a row, and you have another race like what happened in Mexico, where a chance of victory, a chance of the podium, just disappears totally outside of your control, it's tough to deal with. It's very tough to deal with. "So Brazil's a place that I love, I've got great memories of. Do I come in with high expectations? Honestly, no, to be honest. But looking forward to next year for sure. And just continue to work on the things that I can control, and pray that things outside of my control sort themselves out." Russell said he went through every race of 2026 with his engineers and found "we've only had six races this season where we had not an issue". "So 14 [likely 13, as there have been 19 weekends so far] of those races we've had things that have been what we thought was bad luck, but we need to start questioning things more deeply when it's happening so often, and especially on our side. "That was the main feeling for me." So, we put that claim to the test: we've gone through F1 2026's 19 weekends so far and found the following:Russell's campaign started in dream fashion with a dominant victory in the Australian season opener, while Antonelli paid the price for a costly final practice crash that left him compromised for the rest of the weekend on a suboptimal, unrefined set-up. He could probably still count Australia as an 'issue' weekend as he had to fight back from having a depleted battery before he started the race - costing him positions to the Ferraris and requiring him to fight back into the lead. Russell followed it up with a sprint win in China, but his first real bit of bad luck came in grand prix qualifying when his car ground to a halt at the start of Q3. This left him needing a late lap to salvage second on the grid. Reflecting on that session, Russell told media including The Times: "I pulled the clutch half a second too early in the qualifying, which led to my car breaking down. "Should we have known about that? Maybe yes. Maybe not." Russell had been faster than Antonelli all the way through the weekend up to that point, so you can make a case he'd have won there with a normal Q3. At Suzuka, poor safety car timing helped Antonelli to victory and cost Russell a shot at it. But Antonelli looked the faster driver and may have won on sheer pace. It looked more like a fight between him and Oscar Piastri's McLaren.But Russell was also then further compromised on the safety car restart by his car being put into an extra harvesting mode, leaving him fourth at the chequered flag. "Then in Japan, doing the upshift at the exact same time as I clicked another button...on the steering wheel...should we have known about that? Maybe yes. Maybe not," Russell reflected. Antonelli won from pole in Miami while Russell finished fourth on what appeared to be a clean weekend for both cars.Russell and Antonelli then scrapped for victory in Canada when Russell's engine failed while he was leading. Antonelli won again in Monaco while Russell had a double-hit of penalties, the latter for Mercedes not serving his first, a five-second penalty for pitlane speeding, correctly. Given the circumstances of the pitlane speed limit penalties that weekend and Russell being blameless for the second penalty, it was another unlucky weekend and a lost podium (as he was third on the late-race restart). Russell finished second at Barcelona; Antonelli had passed him (and may have challenged Lewis Hamilton for the victory), but his Mercedes broke down with an electrical issue late on.Russell won in Austria, beautifully judging the yellow flags in qualifying while Antonelli mistook double-waved yellows for single ones and backed off, ending up fourth on the grid and third in the race. Russell struggled with power unit deployment issues at Silverstone and Spa. At Silverstone he salvaged second (so probably did not lose any points) while Antonelli loses a likely victory to a front-left wheel-shield failure. At Spa, the issue cost Russell 0.2-0.25 seconds in qualifying, while on the opening lap it left him vulnerable on the Kemmel Straight. This led to contact with Lewis Hamilton, who was penalised for the collision - which put Russell out on the spot. Antonelli won the race from pole. At Hungary, Russell cracked a sump running slightly wide over a kerb in Q3, which left him seventh on the grid prompted engine-swap ramifications down the line. Then in the race he stalled and sank like a stone because of an engine rev anomaly, and an ill-timed virtual safety car stunted his recovery, while Antonelli took third. Antonelli and Russell finished second and third at Zandvoort, while at Monza Antonelli's excellent charge through the field - from 19th, owing to an engine-change grid penalty - was aided by the red flag and another well-timed virtual safety car. Antonelli's pace was so strong he may have still won without those anyway, but he was certainly aided by fortune on Sunday. A virtual safety car helped Antonelli beat Lando Norris's McLaren to victory in Madrid while Russell was fifth, off Antonelli's pace all weekend. Russell won in Baku while Antonelli crashed in qualifying before recovering to fifth. Another power unit failure at Sepang cost Russell a likely podium meant he had to take a grid penalty in Singapore. Russell blew a sprint victory there by crashing out of the lead at the end of the first lap, while he recovered to ninth in the grand prix.Russell picked up a five-second time penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage at Austin and labelled his own pace "rubbish" en route to eighth, while Antonelli won again.Then in Antonelli's title-sealing Mexico weekend, Russell had a deployment issue that dropped him from his front-row start. He clashed with Isack Hadjar's Red Bull and was penalised 10 seconds. So really, there have been 12 weekends where Russell has some publicly disclosed bad luck - 10 of which cost him points - not counting issues that he or the team have not revealed. It is true that this dwarfs Antonelli's misfortune, as he only really lost points to factors outside his control at Silverstone and Barcelona. Ultimately, Russell can only make a case that he lost victories in China (Q3 problem), Canada (power unit failure) and Monza (red flag and VSC timing that helped Antonelli), but even all three of those were far from guaranteed. Maybe Antonelli would've just been quicker even if Russell had a normal qualifying in China, maybe Antonelli would've won their dogfight in Canada, and maybe Antonelli had the pace at Monza to win regardless.We'll never know the answer to those questions, but only the most ludicrously generous estimates of the points Russell has lost this season put him marginally ahead of Antonelli right now, if you then subtract the points Antonelli gains from it. Russell's lost points to bad luck - A (very) generous viewChina - 7 points (1st not 2nd) Japan - 6 points (2nd not 4th)Montreal - 25 points (1st not DNF) Monaco - 15 points (3rd not 12th) Belgium - 15 points (3rd not DNF) Hungary - 6 points (4th not 7th) Italy - 7 points (1st not 2nd) Malaysia - 15 points (3rd not 20th) Singapore - 6 points (6th not 9th) Mexico - 10 points (2nd not 6th) Total = 112 lost points New gap to Antonelli = Russell leads by 6 points *accounting for Antonelli's net points loss as a resultThis would be an impossibly fortunate season for Russell, taking very generous liberties such as assuming he wins in China, Canada and Italy, plus presuming he maintains his second place in Mexico, and crucially not removing of Antonelli's own bad luck. And even in this highly unlikely scenario where Russell is leading by six points, you'd back Antonelli to overturn it comfortably in the final four races on this season's form. In reality, even if you balanced out the reliability dramas of both cars, of which Russell has had more, Russell would still be over 60 points behind Antonelli instead of 130. Russell called it "difficult to put a number on how much [reliability] has impacted the championship" and pointed to one important factor. "It's often about momentum. When we start the season, we had the issue in China with the failure in qualifying, we had the issues in Japan, we had the engine failure in Canada, we had the drivethrough penalty that wasn't a drivethrough penalty in Monaco. These things compound," Russell explained."If you're in the championship fight, or you're within touching distance, you don't feel like you're having to do catch-up. And maybe that contributed towards overdriving and trying to overachieve. Maybe not." Again, we'll never know how a cleaner start to the season would've changed things for Russell or put more pressure on Antonelli. Russell's bigger problem was how quickly Antonelli became the faster Mercedes driver. Has Russell had more bad luck than Antonelli this year? Yes. But has Antonelli been the better, faster driver on more weekends? Absolutely yes. And it's something Russell himself acknowledged in Mexico on the eve of Antonelli's coronation: "The truth is he's been at a higher level than me this year." The bad luck ballooned the gap and made the defeat all the more crushing, but the speed and execution difference this year meant the intra-team fight was only ever going one way.

item.title: EF Education-EasyPost continue post-Carapaz rebuild for 2027 with two more development team graduates
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: The former had started his path to the pros in Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe's junior setup at Team GRENKE-Auto Eder, but joined EF Education-Aevolo for 2026. Despite setbacks due to crashes and injury in the first half of the season, Capello closed out the racing calendar strongly and has now earned the step up he's dreamed of.They join Tao Geoghegan Hart, Ivan Sosa, Nicholas Milesi, Tobias Bayer, and Emil Herzog as EF's new arrivals for 2027. Team boss Jonathan Vaughters had already confirmed that Carapaz's departure was due to overstretched finances, with development team graduates allowing them to bolster their roster size closer to the 30-rider maximum while keeping the costs down"I’m looking forward to the future and not looking back. It’s been my dream to race pro since I started cycling. I can’t wait to race with the best riders in the world, and EF Education-EasyPost is a really cool group," said Capello."I’ve had my fair share of bad luck this season, but I’m confident I’m in a good position to join the WorldTour with EF Education-EasyPost. They have shown a lot of patience and faith in my qualities as a rider, and I’ve worked really hard since joining the development team at the start of the year. I’m confident I can have a successful 2027 with the team and be a strong rider and teammate."Next year I want to try my hand at some short stage races but mostly just gain as much experience as possible. I want to learn from my teammates, and give everything that I can. I can’t wait to start."His best results so far came as a junior in 2025, taking second at the European Championships road race, sixth in the World Championships time trial, and winning the Italian junior ITT title. Despite the injuries, which mostly prevented him from kicking on fully in 2026, EF are still confident in his abilities as a GC prospect."If you see Roberto’s results, he was one of the top riders in 2025. I’m super happy that we signed him," said head of scouting Sebastian Langeveld. "This year was a bit on and off because of injury, but you can see from his training that he’s super talented. He has an incredible capacity on climbs and against the clock. He’s a very promising GC rider. It will take time, maybe a few years, but he has the qualities even though he’s still super young."Hlady rode as a stagiaire for the WorldTour squad back at the end of 2024, and then raced for two seasons on the Aevolo squad to earn his way up to a full spot. A two-time under-23 national road race champion, Hlady also finished on the podium of the elite men's road race at the US national champs in 2025 behind Quinn Simmons and Evan Boyle. "I’m excited to be stepping up and into the next phase of my career with this amazing team," said Hlady. "Honestly, over the last few years, I always thought joining the WorldTour was possible, but I never thought it was guaranteed, so having this opportunity means so much to me. I truly believe that I have more to give and more room to develop as a rider."In 2026, he finished second on a stage of the Alpes Isère Tour, and netted top-10s on stages at the Flèche du Sud and Le Tour de Bretagne Cycliste. For 2027, Hlady is looking to improve on his versatility, with the team confident he can go in any direction when it comes to specialising. "Obviously, EF Education-EasyPost has strong American roots, but even if you took that aspect out of the equation, this is the team that I’d want to join. If you lined up all the teams in the men’s WorldTour, I’d choose EF Education-EasyPost every time," he said."I’m grateful, and I appreciate that we still have this cool international flavour and culture. I think we’re a really diverse team, and what sets us apart is that at the biggest races we always seem to punch above our weight. It’s an all-or-nothing and fun racing attitude. From the outside, they seem like the best team too because all the staff seem really cool too," he added."I want to get stronger, better and faster in every possible way and then see where that takes me. From there, I’ll sit down with the team in November at our next camp, and that’s when we’ll formulate a plan in terms of expectations and race calendar.""Gavin came with Aevolo, and he’s shown throughout the last couple of years, with his national titles, that he has a lot of upward potential. He raced with the WorldTour team this year, and he did really well as a teammate, and he’s ticked a lot of boxes for us this year," added Langeveld."It’s a bit early to determine where he will end up as a rider, but he still has a lot of untapped potential, and we’re going to work with him on getting the best out of himself in the coming season. He can climb, and he might even go in the direction of the classics, but really, it’s about taking our time with the young riders and not rushing them."The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down. item.title: Michael Vanthourenhout fined for post-race clash with Cameron Mason at Middelkerke cyclo-cross
item.author: Owen Rogers
item.content:encoded: Round two of the Superprestige ended in controversy on Thursday evening after series leader Michael Vanthourenhout (Pauwels-Sauzen-Altez Industriebouw) was fined following a post-race altercation.The incident occurred after he clashed with Cameron Mason (777TV) late in the Superprestige race at Middelkerke, the Belgian rider shoulder barging Mason on the eighth of 10 laps of the Nordzeecross circuit.After the race, Vanthourenhout was seen on TV coverage approaching and shouting at Mason, who turned round and remonstrated with the Belgian, the two arguing briefly. Organisers have confirmed to that Vanthourenhout was fined 200 Swiss francs (€218) for the post-race incident.Vanthourenhout had led onto the eighth lap, but was in second place behind eventual winner Joran Wyseure when Mason made a move on a straight section. Seeing the Scottish rider coming up on his left, Vanthourenhout moved out and barged into him, but in doing so seemed to be concentrating too much on Mason and not on the race, losing balance and crashing on the next left hand bend.Consequently, Vanthourenhout dropped back to seventh place and was forced to chase back to the leading group. Meanwhile, Mason also crashed, after failing to negotiate a set of barriers, falling from second to sixth place, Vanthourenhout clearly commenting to the Scot as he passed, pushing him wide on the next bend."It was in the heat of the battle, adrenaline got the better of us," Vanthourenhout said in his post-race interview. "I don't think he should have come on the inside there, but it is a manoeuvre that is allowed. I lost my balance, and from sixth or seventh place it is difficult to get to the front." When asked whether the incident prevented him winning he said: "It plays a role, but that is a race. I was disappointed, but I am also happy that I still made the podium. My second place is good for the standings."For his part, Mason was seen laughing with team staff after the incident, later adding the caption "Something something, 'own medicine' something something. Another solid race. Onto the next" on his Instagram story.The race was a fast one with hectic, exciting racing throughout, Joran Wyseure (Crelan-Corendon) taking the win ahead of Vanthourenhout. Swiss champion Kevin Kuhn (Heizomat-Cube) was third, one place ahead of Mason.Vanthourenhout has had an excellent start to the season, winning four of his seven races to date and never finishing off the podium. Having won the first round of the Superprestige at Overijse on October 25, he started Thursday’s race leading the series, his second place enough to retain his lead in a series where he finished second overall last season. Though not matching his Belgian rival, Mason has also had a good season, with eighth place in the first of six races the lowest placing so far. The two riders will line up against each other at Sunday's European championships, which Vanthourenhout won ahead of Mason in 2023.The road season might be at an end, but Cyclingnews isn't slowing down.
